title: Signed provenance trace hook and fanout-safe propagation shim
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: In multi-hop and fanout scenarios (proxies, edge workers, server->server calls, websockets, gRPC streams) existing trace headers are mutable, which allows intermediaries to alter sampling decisions and provenance metadata. That causes inconsistent sampling, attribution misalignment across services, and makes forensic debugging of high-latency/error traces unreliable. We need a lightweight mechanism to (1) assert minimal provenance integrity, (2) carry a stable sampling decision and origin hints across mixed transports, and (3) be safe in fanout (branching) without exploding header size or adding heavy crypto latency to the critical path.

Goal: Add a signed provenance trace header and an accompanying propagation shim for Redwood SDKs and the runtime ingress/egress middleware that: 1) binds request-level provenance (origin, ingress node id, short TTL) to the trace id, 2) preserves the sampling decision and how it was made (heuristic/service vs. upstream policy), and 3) supports safe fanout by allowing downstream branches to append an attenuated provenance entry without invalidating upstream assertions.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts and verifies signed provenance header (proto v1) and rejects malformed signatures with soft-fail logging (does not drop request).
SDKs emit signed provenance when configured; default off for beta. Flagged rollout via account-level opt-in.
Fanout append semantics implemented: downstream services may add an 'append record' that is verifiable and size-bounded.
Sampling decision consistency: unit tests + integration tests demonstrate consistent sampling decision propagation across HTTP, gRPC, and websocket proxy hops.
Dashboards: new trace integrity metric and rejected-signature rate visible in Observability Console (per-region, per-route).
Performance: median per-request overhead for signing/verifying added by runtime < 0.6 ms P50 (measured on p4d equivalent), and <1.8ms P95.
design_notes: Header format: X-RW-Provenance: base64(payload).signature where payload is JSON-LD compact form with fields: trace_id, ingress_node, ts, ttl, decision, algo_version, nonce-list-summary. We keep payload compact (<= 256 bytes typical).

Signing primitive: Ed25519 for verification efficiency and small signature size (64 bytes). Keys are per-region KMS-managed signing keys. Runtime verifies signatures with cached public keys; SDKs sign with short-lived client keys obtained from control plane (delegated signing token) to avoid shipping private keys to client apps.

Fanout strategy: downstream nodes add a small "append record" blob containing {node_id, ts, reason_code}, signed by that node using its key. Append records are attested but do not mutate the original provenance claim; verifiers accept provenance chains up to N entries (configurable, default 5).

Sampling semantics: the provenance payload carries a canonical sampling decision enum (keep/drop/unknown) plus a provenance tag that indicates whether decision originated here or was inherited. When a verifier sees conflicting decisions it follows: (1) if upstream decision is explicit keep/drop, honor it; (2) if unknown, allow local sampling to decide and append record. This avoids flip-flopping in middle proxies.

Transport compatibility: we map header to HTTP/gRPC metadata and to websocket subprotocol handshake metadata. For binary transports we use base64 envelope. For proxies that cannot carry signature, runtime can fall back to 'signed-envelope' retained at edge and exchanged via out-of-band sticky metadata (short-lived token).

Failure modes: signature verification failure is non-fatal by default but increments a new trace_integrity.alert metric. Admins can opt-in to strict reject mode for high-security customers (enterprise/private).
Privacy: provenance payload avoids PII. Node IDs are short opaque identifiers; control plane maps to human-readable names stored in audit logs accessible to admins.
tradeoffs: Crypto cost vs. integrity: Ed25519 chosen for speed and small size. Adding signing increases CPU on high QPS paths; mitigated via verification caching and hardware acceleration where available.

Header size vs. fanout info: support bounded append records (default max 5) to avoid header blowup. This trades off full lineage visibility for predictable overhead. We will persist full lineage to trace storage when available via async ingress-to-backend supplement.
Soft-fail vs. strict enforcement: default soft-fail to prevent accidental outages. Strict enforcement is available as an opt-in policy for Private/Enterprise deployments.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (beta): implement runtime verification and append support behind a feature flag; SDKs add signing APIs behind an opt-in client config. Release to internal Canary and a handful of opt-in customers. (2 weeks).
Phase 1: enable SDK signing for Redwood-hosted SDKs with control-plane short-lived signing tokens; surface feature in Console with per-account toggle. Collect metrics and error rates. (3 weeks).
Phase 2: enable verification at edge proxies and ingress routers, implement fanout append handling. Provide opt-in strict mode for selected accounts. (2 weeks).
Phase 3: broad rollout, announce in release notes, add migration docs for partner proxies and gateway integrations. Add support for on-prem KMS key material where required. (2 weeks).
testing: Unit tests for header encoding/decoding, signature verification, append-chain limits, and sampling decision precedence rules.
Integration tests across HTTP -> gRPC -> websocket multi-hop chain that include proxies that drop headers mid-path to verify fallback behavior.
Load test: sign/verify microbenchmark on p4d-equivalent with synthetic QPS to verify P50/P95 overhead targets.
Chaos test: inject malformed signatures and network reorderings to validate soft-fail telemetry and no-request-drop guarantee.
End-to-end QA: canary with two internal services and one external partner proxy; confirm dashboards show trace_integrity and rejected_signatures metrics.
metrics_and_dashboards: tracing.sampling.discrepancies.count (cases where downstream sampling overrode explicit upstream keep/drop)
Console dashboard: Trace Integrity Summary panel + per-account rejected signature alert threshold (default 0.1%).
